overview: Cost-effectiveness analysis of offering group antenatal care, using a controlled before-after comparison of the two group-care hubs and the four individual-care hubs, 2024 against 2025 to 2026, from the health service perspective.
population: All women booking antenatal care at the six hubs from January 2024 to June 2026 whose pregnancy ended by December 2026 (about 8,500 women); analysed by hub of booking.
exposure: Booking at a hub that offered group care (the two hubs from January 2025).
procedures: Attendance from the booking system; midwife hours per session from rotas; rooms from the booking system; childcare and interpreters from invoices; unit costs from finance memo FIN-MAT-2026-09. Individual appointment costs from the same sources.

outcomes.name: Incremental cost per additional woman attending eight or more contacts
outcomes.measure: Difference-in-differences in cost per woman booked divided by the difference-in-differences in attendance

outcomes.name: Attendance at eight or more contacts
outcomes.why: The effect in its own right.

outcomes.name: Uptake of group care
outcomes.measure: Proportion of women booked at group-care hubs who attended at least one group session

outcomes.name: Late booking after 16 weeks
outcomes.why: Group scheduling could delay booking for some women.

feasibility: Existing data; 60 finance analyst hours cover costing and the bootstrap analysis.
biasMitigation: Analysis by hub of booking, not by choice
Pre-change trends compared between hub groups
Costs from invoices rather than estimates
Sensitivity analyses for group size and interpreter use

biasFlags.label: Non-random hub selection
biasFlags.note: The two hubs were chosen for deprivation; the before-after contrast handles stable differences only.

biasFlags.label: Changes in comparison hubs
biasFlags.note: Defeating criterion k3; checked with the service's change log.

parsimony.simplestPath: One comparison of hub groups before and after, one ratio with bootstrap uncertainty.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the CHEERS 2022 reporting framework.
summary: Controlled before-after cost-effectiveness analysis by hub of booking.
